report:
Conclusion: the claim is **accurate for U.S. labeling**; the view that it is false is not supported. The FDA label states: “Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years. Replace the system after 5 years if continued use is desired” (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf). DailyMed mirrors the same indication and replacement instruction (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080). Bayer’s 2016 FDA-approval announcement also described Kyleena 19.5 mg as approved “for prevention of pregnancy for up to five years” (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html).

Likely confusion: longer durations belong to some **52 mg** levonorgestrel IUDs (e.g., Mirena/Liletta), not Kyleena’s lower-dose 19.5 mg system. Extended-use literature discusses evidence beyond labeled durations mainly for 52 mg devices and FDA extensions such as Mirena’s, not a Kyleena extension (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0010782422001627). So, absent a new FDA label change, Kyleena remains approved for up to five years; beyond that is off-label/unproven. Outside the U.S., check the local product label.
